claims.text: The targeted material family is Fe-Co-Ni-based FCC high-entropy alloys.
Introducing or varying transition metals with partially filled d orbitals, such as Fe, Co, Ni, or Mn, will increase the orbital magnetic moment contribution.
An increased orbital magnetic moment contribution will enhance saturation magnetization.
Enhanced saturation magnetization will improve magnetic energy density.
Minimizing local lattice distortion prevents orbital quenching.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-based FCC alloy is a random solid solution with high lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch.
HPHT treatment at 1473 K and 6 GPa followed by cooling to room temperature is the proposed processing condition.
HPHT treatment reduces local lattice distortion in Fe-Co-Ni-based FCC alloys.
HPHT treatment and composition tuning promote chemical short-range ordering in Fe-Co-Ni-based FCC alloys.
Chemical short-range ordering and reduced lattice distortion modulate crystal-field splitting.
Severe local lattice distortion and chemical disorder create crystal-field perturbations that quench orbital moments in FCC high-entropy alloys.
Establishing short-range order alleviates orbital-moment quenching.
An unquenched orbital moment contributes constructively to the alloy's total magnetic moment.
The treated alloy will exhibit a measurable increase in orbital magnetic moment relative to an as-cast random solid solution.
The magnetic improvement will occur without sacrificing the mechanical strength of the HEA matrix.
Conventional Fe-Co-Ni FCC HEAs have largely quenched orbital moments and magnetism dominated by spin moments.
The proposed mechanism is not expected to apply to BCC refractory HEAs or to alloys forming brittle phases or undergoing excessive magnetic dilution.
The cited evidence contains no direct measurements of orbital moments or magnetic properties in Fe-Co-Ni FCC HEAs.
The primary state-of-the-art challenge is establishing and quantifying the orbital-moment contribution to saturation magnetization in Fe-Co-Ni FCC HEAs.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits adding Mn, while the conditions and boundary describe the hypothesis as restricted specifically to the Fe-Co-Ni system. A Mn-containing alloy is no longer strictly within the ternary Fe-Co-Ni system unless 'based' is interpreted broadly.
